claim: The paper defines 'prime power pseudoperfect numbers' and 'prime power Giuga numbers' as generalizations arising from varying Egyptian-fraction equations, and shows a sequence of Amarnath Murthy in OEIS is a subsequence of the prime power pseudoperfect numbers.
stance_target: breadth of active Egyptian-fraction-equation variants in the contemporary literature
quoted_support: From varying Egyptian fraction equations we obtain generalizations of primary pseudoperfect numbers and Giuga numbers which we call prime power psuedoperfect numbers and prime power Giuga numbers respectively.
